title: 九年级上学期期中模拟 · 语文
scope: 统编九上前半册：诗歌赏析、议论性表达、岳阳楼记/醉翁亭记；兼顾初中已学古诗文与《水浒传》整本书阅读。未取得学校教学进度，后台可按实际进度调整。
description: 原创整卷练习，按2024北京中考语文五大题、27小题结构编排。书写题在网页中以文字核对替代，纸笔模式可练正楷。
source_note: 试卷总分与时长依据北京官方2025考试安排；内部结构参考公开转载的2024北京语文原卷。现当代阅读材料和题目均原创；古诗文为公版作品。非亦庄实验中学试题，主观题分项标准为练习标准。

questions.stem: 请准确输入活动手记标题“校园微更新观察手记”。纸笔练习时，请用正楷书写；网页输入仅核对字词，书写质量由家长另行检查。
questions.rubric: 标题全部准确得1分；漏字、错字得0分。本题网页不评笔迹。

questions.stem: 上面资料中的字音标注不正确的一项是
questions.passage: 【原创情境】学校开展“校园微更新”观察活动。一个旧自行车棚变成了午间阅读角：保留的木梁承载着校园记忆，新书架让空间焕发活力。同学们筹（chóu）备展览，解剖（pāo）更新方案，斟（zhēn）酌文字，并向低年级同学提供（gōng）讲解。
questions.rubric: 选择正确得2分，选错或未选得0分。
questions.explanation: “剖”读 pōu；其余标注正确。

questions.stem: 结合语境，对“凝聚”的理解最恰当的一项是
questions.passage: 同学们先访问保洁员和图书管理员，记录不同使用者的意见，再讨论共同需求。一次次商量，使“让每个人都能方便阅读”从零散想法变成了大家凝聚的共识。
options: 把所有物品紧紧压在一起
意见完全相同，不再需要讨论
把分散的想法汇合成共同认识
人越来越多，空间越来越拥挤
questions.rubric: 选择正确得2分，选错或未选得0分。
questions.explanation: 这里指不同意见通过交流形成共同认识，而非拒绝继续讨论。

questions.stem: 老师亲自参与过建棚。下列成语在本段中使用不恰当的一项是
questions.passage: 阅读角开放那天，同学们兴致勃勃地挑选图书。墙上的老照片与现代书架相得益彰。小组按图索骥，凭借一张旧照片找到建棚的退休老师。老师回忆往事，讲解员则郑重其事地把他过去的经历称作“纸上谈兵”。
questions.rubric: 选择正确得2分，选错或未选得0分。
questions.explanation: “纸上谈兵”指只空谈理论而不解决实际问题；老师谈的是亲身实践经历，不能这样评价。

questions.stem: 依次概括①②③三项设计的特点，最恰当的一项是
questions.passage: 阅读角的方案围绕三项需求展开：①午间借还书不必到远处的图书馆；②低年级学生不用踮脚就能取到书架上层的书；③临时展览结束后，活动书架可以收起，让空间恢复通畅。
questions.rubric: 选择正确得2分，选错或未选得0分。
questions.explanation: 就近借还是便捷，适合身高是适用，可收起改变空间是灵活。

questions.stem:
下句存在搭配问题，请只改一处，使句子通顺：
“这个阅读角既保留了校园的旧记忆，又改善了同学们课余阅读的便利。”
questions.answer: 这个阅读角既保留了校园的旧记忆，又改善了同学们课余阅读的条件。
questions.rubric: 只把“便利”改为“条件”，使“改善……条件”搭配正确、保留原意，得2分；其他仅改一处且搭配正确、语意一致的表达同样得2分。只发现问题或改后仍不通顺得1分；改变原意或无修改得0分。
questions.explanation: “改善”宜搭配“条件、环境”等名词，只将“便利”换为“条件”即可符合“只改一处”的要求。

questions.stem:
补写结语中横线处的一个分句，使其内容衔接、句式大体一致：
“保留旧木梁，让我们触摸校园记忆；________；设置活动书架，让我们学会灵活利用空间。”
横线内容应涉及“低矮书架”和“照顾不同身高的读者”。
questions.answer: 设置低矮书架，让我们体会对不同读者的关怀
questions.rubric: 写出低矮书架及照顾不同身高读者的内容得1分；“动作+对象，让我们……”句式与上下文衔接得1分。合理表达均可。

questions.stem: 默写：我寄愁心与明月，________。（李白《闻王昌龄左迁龙标遥有此寄》，初中已学复习）
questions.rubric: 准确写出“随君直到夜郎西”得1分，错字、漏字、多字得0分；不因句末标点扣分。
questions.explanation: 诗人托明月寄送对友人的牵挂，默写时注意“君”“郎”等字。

questions.stem: 默写：________，在乎山水之间也。（欧阳修《醉翁亭记》）
questions.rubric: 准确写出“醉翁之意不在酒”得1分，错字、漏字、多字得0分；不因句末标点扣分。

questions.stem: 古诗文常启迪人们在困境中保持希望。请写出一组连续的两句，表达这一思想。要求出自初中教材，且不使用本卷已经出现的诗句。
questions.answer: 沉舟侧畔千帆过，病树前头万木春。
questions.rubric: 两句连续、出自初中课内且符合困境中仍有希望主题，每句准确得1分。可答“山重水复疑无路，柳暗花明又一村”等；使用本卷已有句子不得分。
questions.explanation: 可用新生事物蓬勃发展或困境中出现转机的诗句，答案不唯一。

questions.stem: 诗中的“冰塞川”和“雪满山”既是景象，也是比喻。它们比喻什么？从诗句中找出表现诗人一度迷惘的一个动作。
questions.passage:
【公版古诗】
行路难（其一）
李白
金樽清酒斗十千，玉盘珍羞直万钱。
停杯投箸不能食，拔剑四顾心茫然。
欲渡黄河冰塞川，将登太行雪满山。
闲来垂钓碧溪上，忽复乘舟梦日边。
行路难，行路难，多歧路，今安在？
长风破浪会有时，直挂云帆济沧海。
questions.answer: 比喻人生道路上的艰难险阻；“拔剑四顾”（或停杯投箸）。
questions.rubric: 说明人生/仕途道路上的艰难阻碍得1分；写出“拔剑四顾”或“停杯投箸”得1分。不得仅把阻碍理解为天气。

questions.stem: “闲来垂钓碧溪上，忽复乘舟梦日边”运用了典故；末两句又转向对未来的展望。请结合这些诗句，分析诗人的情感如何从迷惘转向坚定。

行路难，行路难，多歧路，今安在？
长风破浪会有时，直挂云帆济沧海。
questions.answer: 借姜尚垂钓、伊尹梦舟后来受到重用的典故，想到自己仍可能被重用；末两句想象乘风破浪远航，表现冲破困难、实现理想的坚定信心。
questions.rubric: 典故联系被重用/施展抱负得1分；指出迷惘中重新燃起希望得1分；结合乘风破浪形象说明乐观坚定、实现理想的信心得1分。不要求写出人物姓名，但不应误解为追求隐居。

questions.stem: 甲文中“予尝求古仁人之心”的“求”，解释正确的一项是
questions.passage:
【公版文言文】
甲：范仲淹《岳阳楼记》节选
嗟夫！予尝求古仁人之心，或异二者之为，何哉？不以物喜，不以己悲；居庙堂之高则忧其民；处江湖之远则忧其君。是进亦忧，退亦忧。然则何时而乐耶？其必曰“先天下之忧而忧，后天下之乐而乐”乎！噫！微斯人，吾谁与归？

乙：《孟子·尽心上》节选
穷则独善其身，达则兼善天下。
【注】穷：不得志。达：得志。兼：同时。
questions.rubric: 选择正确得2分，选错或未选得0分。
questions.explanation: “求”指探求，整句意为我曾经探求古代品德高尚者的思想感情。

questions.stem: 下列对甲文的理解，不正确的一项是
questions.passage:
【公版文言文】
甲：范仲淹《岳阳楼记》节选
嗟夫！予尝求古仁人之心，或异二者之为，何哉？不以物喜，不以己悲；居庙堂之高则忧其民；处江湖之远则忧其君。是进亦忧，退亦忧。然则何时而乐耶？其必曰“先天下之忧而忧，后天下之乐而乐”乎！噫！微斯人，吾谁与归？

乙：《孟子·尽心上》节选
穷则独善其身，达则兼善天下。
【注】穷：不得志。达：得志。兼：同时。
options: “不以物喜，不以己悲”写古仁人不因外物好坏、个人得失而喜悲。
“是进亦忧，退亦忧”说明古仁人在任何处境中都只关心个人前途。
“然则何时而乐耶”用设问引出古仁人的忧乐观。
“微斯人，吾谁与归”表达作者向往与古仁人志同道合。
questions.rubric: 选择正确得2分，选错或未选得0分。
questions.explanation: “进”忧百姓、“退”忧君，超越了个人前途和得失。

questions.stem: 结合甲乙两则材料回答：在“达”和“穷”两种处境中，两则材料分别提出了怎样的做法？它们共同体现了什么价值追求？
questions.passage:
【公版文言文】
甲：范仲淹《岳阳楼记》节选
嗟夫！予尝求古仁人之心，或异二者之为，何哉？不以物喜，不以己悲；居庙堂之高则忧其民；处江湖之远则忧其君。是进亦忧，退亦忧。然则何时而乐耶？其必曰“先天下之忧而忧，后天下之乐而乐”乎！噫！微斯人，吾谁与归？

乙：《孟子·尽心上》节选
穷则独善其身，达则兼善天下。
【注】穷：不得志。达：得志。兼：同时。
questions.answer: 甲：居朝廷高位关心百姓，远离朝廷仍忧念国事；乙：得志兼济天下，不得志修养自身。共同追求超越个人得失、坚守道德并承担社会责任。
questions.rubric: 甲文两种处境的做法各0.5分，共1分；乙文两种处境的做法各0.5分，共1分；共同点“坚守道德/不计个人得失”得1分、“关怀天下/社会责任”得1分。允许其他有文本根据的概括。
questions.explanation: 比较时既要看到忧天下与善天下的共同点，也要保留“穷则独善其身”这一差异，不把两者简单说成完全相同。

questions.stem: 《水浒传》中的鲁智深和林冲都在遭遇不公后走向反抗，但表现方式不完全相同。请各举一个具体情节，比较两人性格的一处差异，并说明这种差异怎样使“反抗不公”的主题更丰富。（100字左右）
questions.answer: 鲁智深得知金氏父女被欺辱，主动筹钱救助，拳打镇关西，表现急公好义、行动果断；林冲遭陷害起初仍忍让，直到山神庙得知对方要害命才奋起反抗，显示由隐忍到坚决的转变。不同性格的人都被不公逼向反抗，揭示压迫之深。
questions.rubric: 鲁智深具体情节与特点对应得1.5分；林冲具体情节与特点对应得1.5分；明确比较差异得1分；结合社会压迫/正义追求等说明主题得1分。其他准确情节与合理比较也可，不强制使用参考例子。

questions.stem: 根据三则材料，下列说法不符合文意的一项是
questions.passage:
【原创非连续性文本；表内数据为命题设置的模拟调查】
材料一
学校的阅读节不只安排讲座，还邀请学生为“课间十五分钟”设计阅读活动。老师提醒：碎片时间可以用于初读、浏览或复习，但较长作品的深入理解仍需持续阅读；不能把翻过多少页直接当作读懂多少内容。

材料二
九年级两个小组各有20人，用四周试行不同阅读办法。两组阅读同一批文章，在试行前后完成同等难度的概括测试。
甲组：每天课间自主阅读，无讨论；概括测试平均分由6.0分增至6.8分。
乙组：每天课间阅读，每周用20分钟交流并修正概括；平均分由6.1分增至8.0分。
这是一项小规模模拟活动，不能据此推断所有年级、所有作品的效果。

材料三
乙组同学说：“把理由讲给同伴听，才发现自己只记住故事的热闹，没读出变化的原因。”组长把讨论中的疑问整理成便签，夹在书页旁，周末再读。老师据此建议：活动可以从可达到的小目标开始；让个人阅读与同伴交流相结合；为深入阅读留下稳定时间。
options: 课间阅读可承担初读、浏览或复习的任务。
乙组交流时发现了自己理解中的不足。
表内两组在试行前的测试平均分相近。
乙组的模拟结果证明任何学生都应取消独立阅读。
questions.rubric: 选择正确得2分，选错或未选得0分。
questions.explanation: 材料提示样本小且不应普遍推断；乙组也包含个人阅读，并未取消独立阅读。

questions.stem: 阅读全文，概括“我”对修椅子这件事的认识变化：起初重视什么？后来重视什么？
questions.passage:
【原创记叙文】
那把没有上锁的椅子
①初秋，校门旁那把旧木椅被划进了我们的“微更新”项目。它一边高一边低，坐上去总像船在摇晃。我自告奋勇负责修理，想着换几颗螺丝，再刷一层亮漆，照片一定好看。
②周六，做木工的外公带着工具来到学校。他不急着拆椅子，只在旁边站了一会儿。清洁阿姨放下扫帚，坐着把鞋里的沙粒倒出；抱着书的低年级学生挪到椅边，腾出一只手系鞋带。外公问我：“看见没有，它先是一把给人歇脚的椅子。”我随口应了一声，仍在比较两张色卡。
③拆开椅面才发现，摇晃不只因为螺丝松了，后腿有一处裂纹，旧漆下面还藏着凸起的木刺。外公把细砂纸递给我。我推两下就嫌慢，换了一张粗砂纸，刷刷刷，把木面磨出几道深沟。“快不等于合适。”外公握住我的手，带着我顺木纹轻轻推，再让指腹从侧边试过去。细砂纸发出沙沙声，仿佛一条小溪绕过石头。
④午后，太阳把工具的影子缩成一团。我磨完最后一个角，手腕酸得抬不起来，却不敢再用力乱擦。外公扶着新换的椅腿，让我拧螺丝。我终于发现，他一直把力气用在我看不见的地方：在我拧紧时稳住椅身，在我试坐时检查接缝。他留给我的不是一张漂亮的成品照片，而是一件可以慢慢做好的事。
⑤周一，有同学提议为椅子挂块“请勿使用”的牌子，免得新漆被磨花。我差点赞成。午间，清洁阿姨又走来，迟疑着问：“现在还能坐吗？”我看见她掌心上那道被扫帚压出的红痕，忽然想起外公最早的话。我拿走还没挂上的牌子，说：“就是给您坐的。”
⑥几天后，椅面上留了几道轻轻的擦痕。我蹲下去摸，表面依然平整，没有木刺。两个小同学把书放在椅上，像展开两片小小的风帆。我没有去找补漆的刷子，只在项目记录里写下：“今天，椅子在工作。”
⑦展示时，别的小组拍了改造前后的对比照片。我的最后一张照片却没有人摆好姿势：一只放在椅边的水杯，一双舒展开的手，还有一束落在空位上的阳光。我把标题改为“那把没有上锁的椅子”。那束阳光像在等下一个路过的人。
questions.answer: 起初重视刷亮漆、拍好看照片；后来重视安全平整、方便人使用，真正满足他人需要。
questions.rubric: 起初追求外观/展示效果得1分；后来追求安全实用/服务需要得1分。

questions.passage:
【原创议论文】
把“我会了”再问一遍
①完成一道题、看懂一段讲解后，我们常说“我会了”。但熟悉答案并不等于真正理解。对学习而言，能否说明理由、解决变化后的问题，比这一句轻松的判断更重要。因此，我们应当______。
②检验理解，先要把理由说清楚。例如，有位同学记住“一元二次方程可能有两个实数根”，却把所有方程都当成有两个不同实根。直到向同伴解释判别式，他才发现自己漏掉了零和负数的情况。解释让藏在熟悉感里的缺口露出来，并提供修正的起点。
③检验理解，还要把知识放进新情境。理解一道阅读题，不能只背它的答案；当人物处境、叙述角度变化时，仍能找到文本证据，才说明方法可以迁移。变化情境不是故意刁难，而是让知识摆脱对某一例题的依赖。
④不过，检验并非为了追求“从不犯错”。若把每次错误看成能力的终身判决，人反而容易回避尝试。错误只是当前思考留下的一条线索。记录它出现的条件，再选择合适的练习修正，比反复责备自己更能让学习向前。
⑤因此，把“我会了”再问一遍，就是问：“我能说清为什么吗？换一种情况仍会吗？我知道要修正什么吗？”这些问题把模糊的熟悉感变成可观察的行动，也使自信获得坚实的依据。
questions.answer: 在解释理由、迁移运用和修正错误中检验并深化理解

questions.stem: Why did the writer first want to remove the higher temperature?
questions.passage:
【Original passage B】
For three weeks, our class collected weather information from the same corner of the playground. I was in charge of putting the temperatures on a chart. I liked the task because numbers seemed much safer than speaking in front of people.

When we prepared our report, I noticed something strange. One team had written 28 degrees on a cloudy afternoon, while another had written 23. My first thought was that one team had been careless. I wanted to remove the higher number so that the line on my chart would look smooth.

Before I did that, our teacher asked, “What question could help you understand the difference?” I went to the teams. They showed me their notes. The first team had left its thermometer near a sun-warmed wall. The second had measured in the open shade. Neither team had changed its number. The notes helped us discover that the place of a measurement mattered.

We decided to keep both numbers and explain the different conditions. To check our idea, we made two new measurements at the same time the next afternoon. Again, the temperature near the wall was higher. This test did not explain every possible difference, but it gave us useful evidence.

At the presentation, my chart looked less perfect than those of other groups. I was nervous when a classmate pointed at the two lines. Then I explained what we had found. Instead of laughing, she asked how far from the wall we had placed the thermometer. I suddenly felt that questions did not have to be attacks. They could be invitations to think more carefully.

Now I still enjoy drawing charts, but I always leave space beside them for questions. A tidy result is pleasant to look at. An honest result can help us learn.
options: To make the chart look smooth.
To prove the teacher was wrong.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, thick curtains mainly help by ______.
questions.passage:
【Original passage C】
A classroom can be quiet but still feel uncomfortable. One reason may be that a hard floor and bare walls send sounds back into the room. A chair being moved or a pencil being dropped may produce a longer sound than we expect.

When sound reaches a surface, some of it is reflected and some of it is taken in. Soft materials with many small spaces, such as thick curtains, can take in part of the sound. That does not mean they make all sounds disappear. They mainly reduce repeated reflections, helping people hear speech more clearly.

A group of students wanted to find out how materials changed a room's sound. They made the same short sound in an empty classroom and recorded it with a phone in a fixed position. They repeated the test after hanging thick curtains. In the second recording, the sound faded sooner. To make their comparison fair, they kept the phone, the sound source and the doors in the same positions.

However, improving a room's sound is not simply a matter of adding more soft things. Materials must also be safe and easy to clean. questions.stem: Why does the writer compare the two questions in Paragraph 2?
questions.passage:
【Original passage D】
When people think about a useful skill, they often picture something impressive: writing a computer program, playing a difficult piece of music or speaking another language. Asking for help may not appear on the list. Yet it can be one of the most useful skills we develop.

A request for help is different from asking someone to do all the work. Compare two questions: “Can you finish this problem for me?” and “I tried these two steps, but I cannot see why the result changes. Could you help me find the reason?” The second question shows an effort to think, names a difficulty and gives the helper somewhere to begin. It also leaves the learner responsible for the work.

Some students avoid help because they fear looking weak. In fact, a clear question can reveal the opposite. To describe a problem accurately, we have to notice what we know and what we do not know. A student who says “I am confused about the time order in Paragraph 3” may understand more than one who only says “I cannot read English.” Specific questions make a large difficulty manageable.

Timing matters too. Trying alone for a while can strengthen our thinking. But repeating exactly the same unsuccessful step for an hour is not always useful practice. When we can explain what we have tried and where we are stuck, it may be time to ask. The answer might be a small hint rather than a complete solution.

After receiving help, we should return to the task independently. Explain the new idea in our own words, finish the remaining steps and try a similar problem. Without this return, a helpful conversation may become only a short rest from confusion. With it, another person's guidance can become part of our own understanding.

Learning is often described as an individual journey. That does not mean walking every part of the path alone. Knowing how to seek guidance, and how to use it, allows us to take the next step ourselves.
options: To show that helpers should finish homework.
To prove that every problem has two answers.
To suggest that questions must always be long.
To explain what a useful request for help looks like.

questions.stem: How long did the volunteers collect information at first?
questions.passage:
【Original passage】
A Year 9 class decided to learn how the school could waste less food. At first, some students wanted to write a poster immediately: “Please finish everything on your plate.” Their teacher asked them to understand the problem before offering advice.

For one school week, volunteers stood near the collection point after lunch. They did not record names or photograph people. They simply counted the portions of food left over and asked anyone willing to speak one short question: “What made it difficult for you to finish your lunch?”

The answers were different. Some students said they had chosen too much food because they were very hungry before lunch. Others had to leave quickly for a club meeting. A few said they had not known what a dish contained. The volunteers realised that one simple message could not solve every difficulty.

The class suggested three small changes. Students could first choose a smaller portion and return for more if needed. Clubs could start ten minutes later so that students had enough time to eat. The menu could show the main ingredients of each dish. A month later, the volunteers counted the leftovers again to find out whether the changes helped.

Their teacher did not call this a perfect study. The number of students eating at school changed from day to day, and food choices also varied. Even so, the students learnt to listen before judging and to compare results after taking action. A useful school project, they found, does not end with a colourful poster.

题目①：假设你是李华，你们班调查了40名同学的课后复习方式，结果为：只重读笔记20人；重读并做自测12人；重读、自测并向同伴解释8人。请简要描述结果，并向同学提出两条有理由的复习建议。

• What two suggestions would you give, and why?

题目②：假设你是李华，英语社团征集“A Place to Learn Together”的校园空间设计。请描述你的设想，说明学生可以在这里做什么，以及它怎样帮助学习。

• What would your learning place be like?
• What could students do there, and how would it help them?
questions.answer:
① Our survey shows that half of the students only reread their notes. Twelve students also test themselves, while eight explain ideas to others as well. I suggest doing a short self-test after reading because it can show what we have not understood. We should also explain one difficult idea to a partner. Questions from a partner may help us find mistakes and improve our understanding.

② I would like to create a small learning corner beside our library. It would have a quiet reading area and a table for group discussion. Students could read alone first and then share a difficult question with others. A board could show useful methods rather than only correct answers. This place would help us learn to explain ideas, listen carefully and improve our work together.
